items.problem: PointerRoutedEventArgs.GetCurrentPoint()/GetIntermediatePoints() return Microsoft.UI.Input.PointerPoint, but migrated code kept Windows.UI.Input-typed locals/usings, causing CS0029 conversion errors (x5).
items.evidence: session-log: 'error CS0029: Cannot implicitly convert type Microsoft.UI.Input.PointerPoint to Windows.UI.Input.PointerPoint' (x5).
items.covered_at: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md line 91, Namespace Mapping table row '| Windows.UI.Input | Microsoft.UI.Input |'.
items.why_missed: under-emphasized — a single generic table row doesn't surface the concrete pointer build error or the rule 'replace the using and re-type the PointerPoint locals', so the agent left mixed-namespace types and looped on CS0029.
items.proposed_improvement: Reinforce the existing Windows.UI.Input table row with a concrete CS0029 PointerPoint entry in the 'Common build errors' section telling the agent to use `using Microsoft.UI.Input;` and re-type PointerPoint/PointerPointProperties locals (don't keep a stale Windows.UI.Input using).
items.generalizes: Every migrated pointer handler calls GetCurrentPoint(); the namespace/type mismatch recurs whenever the stale UWP input using survives the rewrite.

items.problem: Windows.UI.Colors references fail with CS0234 (x8) because the Colors palette moved while the Windows.UI.Color struct did not.
items.evidence: session-log: 'error CS0234: The type or namespace name Colors does not exist in the namespace Windows.UI' (x8); fixes use Microsoft.UI.Colors.<Name>.
items.covered_at: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md line 92, Namespace Mapping table row '| Windows.UI.Colors | Microsoft.UI.Colors |'.
items.why_missed: buried — the row is correct but the agent repeatedly hit CS0234 because the easy-to-miss distinction (Colors class moves, Color struct stays) isn't spelled out as a build error.
items.proposed_improvement: Add a one-line CS0234 'Colors' bullet to the pointer/gesture build-error subsection clarifying Colors -> Microsoft.UI.Colors while the Windows.UI.Color struct stays.
items.generalizes: Color literals (Colors.X) appear in nearly every XAML-adjacent code-behind; the CS0234 surfaces broadly after the rewrite.
